page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon 8175M processors running at 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying on external storage options and delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the weak category, representing the bottom 25% of tested systems. However, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores reach average levels. Memory bandwidth for large-block read-only operations is strong, placing in the top 25%, while small-block reads and large-block writes perform at average levels.

This server is configured for workloads requiring high memory capacity and multi-threaded execution rather than raw single-threaded speed. It achieves average throughput in Redis SET operations, static web serving, and software compilation. Large-model LLM inference and text generation tasks show weak performance, making it less optimal for intensive AI generation. Appropriate workloads include database operations, multi-threaded web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from its balanced resource density.
